name: Kimai
description: Kimai — the self-hosted open-source time tracker. Read and create timesheets, browse customers, projects, activities and users, and check the running clock. REST API v1 on your own Kimai instance, bearer API token.
instructions:
**Getting a token** (Kimai 2.x)
1. Sign in to your Kimai instance, open your user profile and go to the **API** tab.
2. Create an **API token** and copy it into `KIMAI_API_TOKEN`. Kimai 2.x uses a bearer token here; the older `X-AUTH-USER`/`X-AUTH-TOKEN` header pair from Kimai 1.x is deprecated and is not what this adapter sends.
3. Set `KIMAI_URL` to the base URL of your instance *without* a trailing slash and without `/api`, e.g. `https://time.example.com`. The adapter appends `/api`.

**Permissions follow the user.** A token for a normal user only sees that user's timesheets. To report across the team, issue the token for a user with the `view_other_timesheet` permission — otherwise the answers will look quietly, wrongly small.

**Kimai is self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector does not offer a trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`kimai.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard will refuse the call before it is made.

**Dates** are ISO 8601, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00`. `begin` and `end` on the timesheet list filter the entry's start time.

**Writes**: `kimai_create_timesheet` books real time. `kimai_stop_timesheet` closes a running entry, which is not undoable from the API.

tools.name: kimai_get_version
tools.description: Read the Kimai version and copyright of the connected instance. No parameters and no permissions needed — the fastest proof that URL and token are both right.

tools.name: kimai_list_timesheets
tools.description: Read timesheet entries in a date range with their project, activity, duration, rate and billable flag. The core reporting query.

user.description: User id to filter by, or `all` to include everyone (needs view_other_timesheet).

exported.description: 0 for not yet exported, 1 for exported.

tools.name: kimai_get_active_timesheets
tools.description: Read the entries that are running right now for the authenticated user — Kimai's live clock, answering 'am I still tracking something'.

tools.name: kimai_list_customers
tools.description: List customers with their number, country, currency and visible flag. Customers are the top of Kimai's customer → project → activity hierarchy.

tools.name: kimai_list_projects
tools.description: List projects, optionally for one customer, with their budget, time budget and start and end dates.

tools.name: kimai_list_activities
tools.description: List activities — the task types time is booked against — either global or attached to one project.

project.description: Restrict to one project id, or `null` for global activities only.

tools.name: kimai_list_users
tools.description: List Kimai users with their username, alias, e-mail and roles. Needs the view_user permission on the token's account.

tools.name: kimai_create_timesheet
tools.description: Book a timesheet entry against a project and activity. Writes to the live instance; omit `end` to start a running entry instead of a closed one.

end.description: Entry end, ISO 8601. Leave empty to start a running entry.

user.description: User id the entry belongs to. Defaults to the token's own user.

tools.name: kimai_stop_timesheet
tools.description: Stop a running timesheet entry, setting its end to now. Not undoable through the API — the entry then has to be edited in the Kimai UI.

id.description: Numeric id of the running timesheet entry.
